subject: HelixPay renewal kickoff — capacity, term, and QBR window
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Sara Vance <sara@helixpay.com>, Tim Lewis <tim.lewis@helixpay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HelixPay renewal kickoff — capacity, term, and QBR window

Hi Sara / Tim —

Quick kickoff to get alignment as we head into your July renewal. Goals for this thread: confirm term and committed capacity options, lock a QBR window for the renewal review, and agree on next steps for the contract/redlines.

Proposed timeline (90-day runway):
- By 6/20: confirm target term (12 vs 24 months) and committed GPU units
- By 6/28: draft SOW and pricing options delivered to HelixPay
- Week of 7/8: QBR + renewal decision meeting (pick 2 candidate slots)
- By 7/15: finalize contract and PO cadence

Ben will outline pricing tiers; Monica will coordinate technical capacity and migration concerns. I attached a first-draft SOW and a QBR calendar invite stub.

Quick ask: can you share the internal stakeholder list (security/finance) who should be included in the QBR and any preferred blackout dates in July?

Thanks —
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: Renewal_SOW_v1.pdf (pdf))
(Attachment: QBR_calendar.ics (ics))
From: Sara Vance <sara@helixpay.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Lewis <tim.lewis@helixpay.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2029 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixPay renewal kickoff — capacity, term, and QBR window

Thanks Rafael — appreciate the clear timeline. A few quick notes from our side:

- Stakeholders: finance (Anika Shah, anika.shah@helixpay.com), infra lead (Zoe Park, zoe.park@helixpay.com), and security (Marcus Chen, marcus.chen@helixpay.com). We’ll include them on the QBR invite once we pick a slot.
- Capacity: our 2029 forecast shows a ~2.4x increase in peak token throughput over the next 12 months. We’re evaluating whether a committed pool (steady) + burst plan (on-demand) is best.
- Term preference: lean toward 24 months if the committed pricing delta is favorable; otherwise 12 months.

Availability for QBR: 7/9 morning (PST) or 7/10 afternoon (PST). Prefer a 60-minute slot.

Couple of questions for Ben/Monica: can you confirm whether we can stage a read-only KV cache snapshot to reduce warm-start latency during batch inference? Also — any outage SLO credits in the event of sustained latency breaches?

Sara
Head of AI Ops, HelixPay
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sara Vance <sara@helixpay.com>, Tim Lewis <tim.lewis@helixpay.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Jun 2029 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HelixPay renewal kickoff — capacity, term, and QBR window

Sara — good notes, thanks. Short answers and next steps: 

- KV cache snapshot: yes — we can support a read-only prefix/KV snapshot approach for warm-starts. Monica, I’ve copied you to coordinate the exact snapshot cadence and expected size.
- SLO credits: we offer defined SLAs on Dedicated plans. For Hosted, we provide latency/uptime targets and can include credit language in the contract for multi-hour incidents. I’ll surface example SLA language in the SOW.

Attached is a pricing summary with three tiers: Core (12-month commit), Growth (24-month commit, discounted), and Burst (on-demand overlay). I highlighted the committed GPU throughput and token-unit pricing per tier.

Proposed QBR slots based on your availability:
- Tue 7/9 09:00–10:00 PDT
- Wed 7/10 14:00–15:00 PDT

Next actions I’ll take: update SOW with SLA language and committed unit schedule, draft pricing scenarios for 12 vs 24 months, and send updated calendar invites.

Best —
Ben Carter
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: HXP_pricing_summary_v1.xlsx (xlsx))
From: Tim Lewis <tim.lewis@helixpay.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Sara Vance <sara@helixpay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Jun 2029 16:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HelixPay renewal kickoff — capacity, term, and QBR window

Thanks team. A couple of procurement points from my side: 

1) For a 24-month committed price, what’s the escalation cadence (annual vs CPI)? We need predictability for our FY31 budgeting.
2) Can you provide a redline-friendly Word version of the SOW — our legal team prefers tracked changes.

Also: assuming we pick the Growth (24-month) tier, can you include a 30% burst headroom in the pricing model (i.e., committed + 30% burst) and a one-time onboarding credit to cover migration costs? If so, call out where that shows up in the SOW.

I’m leaning to take the Wed 7/10 14:00 slot.

-Tim
VP, Engineering, HelixPay
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Tim Lewis <tim.lewis@helixpay.com>, Sara Vance <sara@helixpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 Jun 2029 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: HelixPay renewal kickoff — capacity, term, and QBR window

Perfect — thanks Tim. Taking the action items and next steps: 

- Ben: produce redline-friendly SOW (Word) and updated pricing with 24-month Growth tier including 30% burst headroom and a one-time onboarding credit. Deliver by Tue 6/18 EOD.
- Monica: confirm KV snapshot cadence and draft appendix on warm-start architecture and expected latency gains. Deliver by Tue 6/18 EOD.
- Rafael (me): send provisional calendar invite for Wed 7/10 14:00–15:00 PDT and loop in Anika/Shah and Marcus/Chen from HelixPay. I’ll also open the HubSpot deal and attach the SOW link.

To Sara/Tim — please accept the 7/10 invite when it arrives. If anything blocks the 7/10 slot, flag it here and we’ll pivot to 7/9 morning.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the QBR and finishing the renewal.

Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: Renewal_SOW_v1.docx (docx))
(See HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/3821)
